claims.text: The target material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The high-temperature specimen contains 1 wt.% oxygen.

An approach combining ab initio defect-dependent scattering parameters, machine learning, and effective-medium theory will predict electrical conductivity more accurately than traditional analytical predictions.
The proposed accuracy advantage applies across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Quantum effects and carrier localization are significant in HfNbTaTiZr over 0–200 K.
Thermal activation and impurity scattering dominate conductivity behavior over 300–1200 K.
Oxygen impurities and their associated lattice defects alter scattering rates and carrier mobility.
Directly modeling quantum localization at low temperature and phonon and impurity scattering at high temperature will make predicted conductivity reflect real microstructural imperfections.
Idealized analytical models ignore relevant real-world microstructural imperfections.
Traditional analytical predictions for this material are based on perfect, defect-free crystals.
Neglect of defect- and impurity-induced scattering causes errors in existing analytical predictions.
The integrated approach will have a significantly smaller prediction error than traditional analytical predictions.
At 350 K, the model prediction for the oxygen-containing sample will closely match experimental conductivity.
The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr produced by typical processing routes and containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach is applicable only within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K, with accuracy outside those ranges not guaranteed.
Cryogenic defect-scattering parameterization may introduce additional prediction variability.

contradictions.description: The material and conditions fields restrict the 1 wt.% oxygen specimen to the high-temperature regime, while the boundary and falsification design extend the same oxygen-containing sample scope to cryogenic measurements. The intended oxygen content of the 0–200 K specimen is therefore internally inconsistent or at least unresolved.
